newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WEST INDIES COLLAPSE IN FIRST FINAL V PAKISTAN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WEST INDIES COLLAPSE IN FIRST FINAL V PAKISTAN.

text.p: The West Indies' batting lineup collapsed for the second time in five days on Saturday, falling to 179 for nine in 50 overs against spirited Pakistani bowling in the first match of the World Series limited overs final.
The failure of left-handed batting maestro Brian Lara, who had scored 295 runs in his last three innings, was the feature of the collapse.
This match is the first in the best-of-three final series.
Lara's dismissal for nought, caught and bowled by leg-spinner Shahid Afridi, appeared to shock his fellow batsmen, who fell in quick succession after him with a series of tentative shots.
Afridi and aggressive fast bowler Waqar Younis ran amok in a 10-over period starting in the 26th over, taking six wickets between them for only 23 runs.

The procession of batsmen to and from the dressing room was an uncanny replay of the West Indies' display against Pakistan on the same ground on Tuesday, when they lost eight wickets for 25 runs in 11 overs batting first.
Pakistan won that match by eight wickets, chasing a paltry 181 with 64 balls to spare.
The West Indies had begun well after being put into bat by Pakistani captain Wasim Akram, with openers Junior Murray (48) and Sherwin Campbell (52) carefully compiling 99 runs for the first wicket.
But when Murray was caught and bowled by leg-spinner Mushtaq Ahmed and Lara fell, the West Indies retreated into their shells and paid the price.
Waqar was the best of the Pakistani bowlers, taking three wickets for one run in one devastating nine-ball spell. He finished with four for 43 and seemed to improve as the match went on.

Afridi, a teenager who burst on to the world cricketing stage last year with a one-day century, was also dangerous and was virtually mobbed by his ecstatic teammates after plucking the return catch from Lara off his shoelaces.
The youngster will also take on the responsibility of opening the Pakistani innings with world-cup hero Inzamam-ul-Haq.
Afridi takes over from dashing left-hander Aamir Sohail who was suspended for one match for voicing dissent in Pakistan's loss to Australia on Thursday.
Pakistan and West Indies made the best-of-three match finals series when host nation Australia was last week eliminated from the annual tri-nation competition for the first time since 1979/80.

West Indies went into the match as favourites, given their three wins from four matches against Pakistan, but their meagre total of 179 has turned the tables and Pakistan must be confident of repeating their successful run-chase of Tuesday.
